scenarios.description: Recall API design decisions made across multiple sessions.

content.compact_summary: Designed the authentication API. Using JWT tokens with RS256 signing. Access tokens expire in 15 minutes, refresh tokens in 7 days. Tokens are stored in httpOnly cookies, not localStorage (XSS prevention). Rate limiting set to 100 requests/minute per user.

Designed the pagination strategy. All list endpoints use cursor-based pagination, not offset-based (better performance on large datasets). Cursor is an opaque base64-encoded string. Default page size is 25, max is 100. Response format includes next_cursor and has_more fields.

scenarios.description: Learn from corrections about API design mistakes.

content.compact_summary: User corrected: don't return 200 OK for errors — always use appropriate HTTP status codes. 400 for validation, 401 for auth, 404 for not found, 409 for conflicts. The response body should include an error code, message, and optional details field.
User corrected: never expose internal IDs in URLs — use UUIDs instead of auto-incrementing integers. Also never include sensitive data in query parameters (they get logged); use request body instead.

User corrected: all API endpoints must be idempotent. POST for create should use an idempotency key header. PUT should be a full replacement, PATCH for partial updates. DELETE should be idempotent (return 204 even if already deleted).

scenarios.description: Accumulate deep knowledge about a codebase's architecture.

content.compact_summary: Explored the sift codebase. It has 10 crates: sift-core (types, config), sift-cli (CLI commands), sift-store (vector + FTS storage), sift-memory (knowledge graph), sift-embed (embedding models), sift-mcp (MCP server), sift-server (HTTP API), sift-sources (file discovery), sift-parsers (30+ format parsers), sift-chunker (text splitting).

Learned that sift-memory uses SQLite with WAL mode and a bi-temporal data model (observed_at vs valid_from/valid_until). The MemoryStore struct holds a Mutex<Connection> and a HybridSearchEngine. Recall uses RRF fusion of BM25 + vector results.

questions.answer: Bi-temporal model with observed_at and valid_from/valid_until

scenarios.description: Remember performance characteristics and bottlenecks.

content.compact_summary: Profiled the search pipeline. The embedding step takes 15ms per query (ONNX CPU inference). BM25 search takes 2ms. Vector search (HNSW) takes 5ms. The RRF fusion and post-filtering takes <1ms. Total recall latency is ~25ms for a typical query with 1000 observations.

Identified memory bottleneck: the consolidation engine holds the SQLite mutex for its entire duration. With 10K observations, consolidation takes ~2 seconds, blocking all other writers. Future optimization: batch updates in a single transaction and minimize lock hold time.

questions.answer: Holds the SQLite mutex for its entire duration, blocking writers
